proposal: The Mandate says protection of American and foreign journalists at USAGM networks and grantees was lacking, and that career officials resisted measures pushed by political appointees: letting threatened broadcasters work from remote locations under federal law enforcement protection, and requiring foreign-based journalists in high-risk countries to tell the agency where they are so they can be rescued, extracted or housed safely. status_summary: No federal action adopting the location-reporting or protected-remote-broadcast measures was found. After Executive Order 14238 (signed 2025-03-14) named USAGM for reduction to its statutory minimum, USAGM placed most staff of the agency and its networks on administrative leave from 2025-03-15, and an AP report of 2025-04-06 said, citing press-freedom groups, that at least 84 USAGM journalists on US work visas could face deportation, while a court had temporarily halted contract terminations. A House Oversight letter to Lake dated 2025-06-17, citing the Mandate's page 241, said USAGM did not know the locations of foreign-based journalists in high-risk countries and requested records; it is a congressional inquiry, not an agency measure. The rating is not_started on the recommended measures; the staff reductions pursue a different recommendation and are noted as context rather than treated as divergence.

timeline.event: USAGM announced that, under the 2025-03-14 executive order, most affected staff of USAGM, Voice of America, the Office of Cuba Broadcasting and grantees would be placed on paid administrative leave.

The Associated Press reported that at least 84 USAGM journalists on work visas could face deportation after the cuts, that a court had temporarily halted contract terminations, and that 11 USAGM-affiliated journalists were jailed abroad; the State Department said it was coordinating with USAGM on imprisoned journalists.

Senators Shaheen and Van Hollen wrote to the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security asking them to protect USAGM-affiliated journalists who could be forced back to authoritarian home countries and to press for jailed colleagues' release; the departments did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

House Oversight Chairman Comer and a subcommittee chair wrote to Lake that USAGM reportedly did not know the locations of foreign-based journalists in high-risk countries, citing the Mandate, and requested insider-threat, visa and other records.
timeline.source: House Oversight Committee (letter via Fox News)

title: Adopt and enforce basic journalist safety measures at USAGM and its grantees
uncertainties: No USAGM or grantee measure adopting location reporting for journalists in high-risk countries or protected remote broadcasting was found. After Executive Order 14238 of 2025-03-14, USAGM placed most staff on leave, and a House Oversight letter of 2025-06-17 said the agency did not know where foreign-based journalists in high-risk countries were; neither is an agency safety measure. Federal Register searches returned nothing, though an agency-filtered query failed; the Journalist Protection Act (H.R. 3203) does not address USAGM; the usagm.gov news page showed one unrelated item and older releases were not read; one news search found 2025 reporting only. USAGM appears in the reginfo.gov agenda selector, but its list could not be reached by code. Internal security directives may be unpublished. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
